$comment: The element map for tools/mockdiff.mjs: for each (mock frame -> app state) pair,
which mock element is which app element. `mock` is scoped to the frame automatically
(`.hdr` means `#S1 .hdr`); `app` is a live-DOM selector, a data-role wherever one exists.
`mock` at FRAME level overrides which mockup frame the entries are read from — several
app states share one drawn frame (S2 draws the overflow menu open, the compile-error
strip and a healthy rail at once, which no single app state can be in).
`hoverOnly` entries are compared in the :hover state only, because the mock paints that
state permanently (`.tile.hov .actions`). `hoverMock`/`hoverApp` say what to put the
pointer ON when that is not the element itself.
FRAME S7c IS RETIRED (Gitea #740/#741, 2026-09-25). It drew the sprite TOOL ROW over
the scene stage, the 16-cell palette grid and the dead `black pixels · sprites are
always keyed` line — every one of which the redesign deleted: a sprite is its own
record with its own editor screen now, a sprite layer MOVES on the stage like every
other layer, and the palette cap is 255 enforced in one function. The mock is what is
wrong here, not the app, so the entry is gone rather than retargeted; the sprite
editor has no mock to diff against (it is the one screen Jeremy asked to be redesigned
from the complaint list rather than from a drawing).
FRAMES S8c AND S8d ARE NOT MAPPED, AND MUST NOT BE (#787, 2026-09-27). They are not
screens: they are a DECISION DRAWING. The two of them draw option A and option B of one
semantic — what the ramp does outside the stops — side by side so Jeremy could pick one,
and their card header reads `A · clamp both ends` / `B · black above the last stop` where
every other frame's reads `Color ramp`. Nothing in the app is or should ever be in that
state. Jeremy picked A on 2026-09-27, so the app clamps at BOTH ends, and the semantic is
pinned where a semantic belongs rather than in a CSS diff: the engine's own test
`palette_lut_clamps_above_the_last_stop_and_below_the_first`
(crates/luxel-core/src/outpipe.rs), `web/tests/paletteLut.test.mjs` (the wasm table against
the browser's synchronous fallback, so the two cannot drift) and `web/tests/gradient.test.mjs`
"the ramp CLAMPS at both ends". The batch-7 block's hatched `.rezone` rule is option B's
and is dead with it — it is drawn in S8d and nowhere else.
THE S8 BATCH, and where each drawn card is measured (#787, 2026-09-27): S8a/S8b/S8g are the
Settings mount at 760 / 760 / 390, S8e/S8f the scene layer's row collapsed and expanded.
S8h and S8i each draw SEVERAL states of one control stacked under `.statecap` captions, so
they are split the way S2 is: `S8h-empty` / `S8h-min` / `S8h-cap` and `S8i-live` /
`S8i-save` / `S8i-clear`, each naming the drawn frame with a frame-level `mock` and picking
its card with `mockNth`. Those two frames draw the card BARE in the frame's 20px padding,
where the Settings mount nests it in `.disclist > .dbody` — 30px narrower — so their
full-width children carry a `box width` allow; S8a draws the nesting and measures 0 on it.
The three S8h states each POST their own palette to the mirror (the `strip` seed's ramp is
the four-stop Sunset every other S8 frame quotes) and they are LAST in this file on purpose:
all frames of a target share one `luxel serve`, so a frame that rewrites the device's ramp
must not run before one that reads it. Every other ramp frame re-POSTs the seeded ramp in
its own first step, which makes each of them a named state rather than a position in a
queue — the same reason `freshProfile` exists.
`allow` lists the deviations Jeremy asked for that the mocks do not show. Each is
`<element>` (the whole element), or `<element>.<property>`. They are printed in the
report as ALLOWED and never counted as deltas.
A `data-role` that stops being UNIQUE silently retargets an entry. A page that grows
a second element with a role the map already names (2026-09-27: `pages/Scenes.svelte`
gained a page bar whose `new-scene` sits above the empty state's, #785) makes the
app-side selector match the FIRST one, and the report is a scrambled "reading order"
delta on an element that did not move. Give the new one its own role, or qualify the
map's selector — do not add an `allow`, because nothing is actually deviating.
`nth` / `mockNth` are 0-BASED INDEXES into the matches, not ordinals. An index
past the end reports "NOT FOUND: <selector>" (which reads like a bad selector),
and an off-by-one silently measures the element next door and PASSES.
SELECTOR TRAP, both sides: `:first-of-type` / `:nth-of-type(k)` count SIBLINGS OF
THE SAME TAG, not members of a class. `.srow`, `.ctlrow`, `.prow`, `.orow`, `.field`,
`.rsec`, `.group` and `.plrow` are all plain <div>s among other plain <div>s, so
`.srow:nth-of-type(2)` is the SECOND DIV — usually not the second `.srow`. Use the
bare class plus `mockNth`/`nth` (an index over the matches) instead. `.sect` in S3
is a real <section> and is the one place `:nth-of-type` means what it looks like.
$seeds: What each MIRROR holds before the frames are measured. A bare `luxel serve` has an
empty library and a stopped playlist, so a Patterns page would have no tiles and a
Playlist page no rows. Names and counts follow the mocks (S1 shows `On device 5`,
S1b shows six bars, S4 four rows). Durations are deliberately huge: the playing tile
and the playing row must be the SAME one for the whole run.
Mirrors only — a real board reached with --device is never written to.
